chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man has completed the two testimonies (of faith), his prayer is considered complete; so if he is in a hurry for a matter he fears might be missed, he may say the final salutation (taslim) and depart, and that will suffice for him."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It sufficed for him / was accepted.
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَانِ: The two testimonies of faith (La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur rasulullah), here referring to the concluding recitation in prayer.
key_terms.مَضَتْ صَلَاتُهُ: His prayer has passed/been completed (considered valid).

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement to validly conclude a prayer if one is in a hurry?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *qasr* or brevity in prayer when necessity (*darurah*) or haste (*hur*) demands it, affirming that completing the two testimonies (al-shahadatayn) suffices for validity. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility within ritual obligations, allowing the worshipper to conclude with the final salutation and depart if they fear missing an important matter, thereby balancing spiritual devotion with practical exigencies.
